7.3.3.a
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.

interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**MRI Report:** The mpMRI prostate showed a focal hypointense lesion in the right peripheral zone apex, demonstrating restricted diffusion with corresponding high signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging showed early arterial enhancement. There was no extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. The impression was PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone apex, approximately 12 mm, with a prostate volume of 26.91 mL, clinical stage cT2a, and a csPCa predicted probability of 0.8577571.
**Pathology Report:** Two biopsy specimens were reviewed. Both revealed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. Perineural invasion was not observed. The histological findings remained stable across both biopsy timepoints.
**Previous Notes:** On 14 Oct 2024, the patient presented with a PSA of 7.0 ng/mL. A biopsy was performed, and pathology confirmed Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2 adenocarcinoma in the peripheral zone, apex right. The patient was referred to urology for specialist assessment.
**Family History:** No relevant family history of prostate cancer was recorded.
**PSA Trend:** The PSA level has shown a trajectory of increasing values: 3.4 ng/mL in Sep 2022, 4.9 ng/mL in Jul 2023, 7.0 ng/mL in Apr 2024, and 10.0 ng/mL in Feb 2025.
**Laboratory Results:** The most recent PSA is 10.0 ng/mL (25 Jan 2025). Creatinine is 157 umol/L, and eGFR is <60 mL/min/1.73m2. Free PSA is 1.31 ng/mL (13%).

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific details regarding the prior PCa diagnosis and treatment plan beyond the initial referral are not fully documented. The specific details of the patient's current active treatment status are not explicitly detailed in the notes.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
This supports the need to address the clinical significance of the rising PSA trend and the high PI-RADS 5 finding in the peripheral zone apex, especially in the context of the confirmed Gleason 3+4 disease.
